# Payment Setup

Builds a nested Payment Instruction for a MyOS customer payment or account-to-account payment. `build` resolves declared parties, prepares payment terms and request bindings, and stores the instruction at the configured destination. Creating an instruction does not confirm funding or payment execution.

## Configuration and parties

`paymentMethod` is read from `/clauses/<clauseKey>/paymentMethod`. It must be `myos-customer` or `myos-account-to-account`; other values fail with `MYOS_PAYMENT_METHOD`. Parameters come from `/clauses/<clauseKey>/parameters`:

- `recipient` identifies the receiving party. Its resolved channel overrides `payee`, including any explicitly supplied `payee`.
- For `myos-account-to-account`, `payer` must also resolve to a declared party. Equal resolved payer and recipient `myosAccountId` values are rejected with `MYOS_SAME_ACCOUNT`. For `myos-customer`, `payer` is a channel name and defaults to `customer`.
- `guarantor` defaults to `guarantor`. A different selected role is also copied into the child’s canonical `guarantor` party and channel; `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel` remains `guarantor`.
- `amountMinor` defaults to `0`. A positive supplied value takes precedence; otherwise the amount is read from the document path supplied by `bindings.amount`. The resulting amount must be an integer from 1 through 1,000,000,000,000. `currency` defaults to `EUR` and must be nonempty text. Amounts use that currency’s minor units.
- `recipientApprovalRequired` defaults to `false` and is copied into payment terms. `parties` defaults to `[]`, selecting all parent activation parties; a nonempty list selects only those roles. `readers` defaults to `[]`, selecting no additional named readers. Selected names must exist in the parent activation roster or readers.
- `instructionClauses` defaults to `{}`. It adds child clauses and can replace the default `method` clause. Keys `activation` and `payment` are reserved.

These are the accepted parameter names, together with `payee`; unknown names are rejected. Payer, resolved payee and selected guarantor must exist in `/activation/parties` and remain included in the child. Their role names, and added clause keys, must be nonempty and contain none of `/`, `~` or `.`.

`resolveParty` first treats text matching a key in `/activation/parties` as that role. Otherwise it accepts a nonempty account-ID string or an object containing a nonempty text `myosAccountId`; the account must match exactly one declared party, whose `/contracts/<role>` entry must exist. Missing accounts, ambiguous or unmatched routes, and missing channels are rejected. The direct role-name branch bypasses these account and channel checks. Recorded party snapshots come from the declared roster, rather than from a supplied candidate object.

## Construction and identity

Construction invokes `requireActive`, passing `call/channel` when `sourceMode` is `workflow`; that guard’s detailed checks are not supplied. `bindings.instruction` supplies the destination path, with no default path established here.

The child receives `paymentDetails.method` and resolved party snapshots in `paymentDetails.parties`: `recipient` for both methods and `payer` for account-to-account payments. Its `paymentTerms` contain the resolved `payerChannel`, `payeeChannel`, a single initial `allowedPayees` entry, `currency`, `recipientApprovalRequired`, and equal initial `amountMinor` and `limitMinor`. `captureGate` is set to an empty string. These amounts describe terms, not balances or confirmed transfers.

Child activation is prepared with `frozen: true`, selected parties and readers, party transports, and references to the parent’s activation access documents. Preparation does not itself prove that the child is active.

The instruction identity is retained at `/connectionState_<clauseKey>/instructionIdentity` and copied to the child’s `instanceKey`. After initial checks, an existing destination with the matching identity returns `created: false`, `outcome: duplicate` and `path`, without replacing or comparing its terms. A different identity fails with `PAYMENT_DESTINATION_CONFLICT`. New construction stores the identity and child and returns `created: true`, `outcome: acceptedNew` and `path`.

## Request bindings

Bindings under `/clauses/<clauseKey>/bindings` are transferred to the child’s payment clause for `approveRecipient`, `requestAuthorize`, `requestCapture`, `requestRefund`, `requestVoid`, `requestPayeeAssignment`, `requestTransactionDetailsUpdate`, `requestFinalAmountResolution`, and the `requestPaymentCompletionLock`, `requestPaymentCompletionUnlock`, `requestPaymentReversalLock`, `requestPaymentReversalUnlock`, `requestTransactionDetailsUpdateLock` and `requestTransactionDetailsUpdateUnlock` actions.

Source scope `in` defaults to `instruction`, so paths refer to the child instruction. Explicit `agreement` sources support `event`, `change`, `embedded` and `collection`; agreement-scoped `workflow` sources are rejected. Agreement events become embedded sources at the child’s `/sources/order`, and other agreement paths are prefixed with `/sources/order`. This requires `/contracts/initialized` in the containing document and adds a reference to it. Timer bindings apply source conversion to `afterEvent` and `cancelOn`, allowing those sources to override the enclosing scope. Detailed payment-action guards and outcome processing are not established by the supplied request-action definitions.

## Method behavior

`myos-customer` creates a MyOS Customer Payment Instruction and sets `paymentTerms.initiationGate` to `/customerSession/funded` in that child. Missing funding state does not establish that funding succeeded or failed. The child declares `provideSession` and `confirmFunding` on channel `guarantor`, and `requestCustomerFunding` on the literal channel `payer`. Their requests identify a session with nonempty `sessionId`; `provideSession` permits omitted `expiresAt` to use an execution-time default whose value is not supplied. The session transitions and gate enforcement are not defined in the supplied implementations.

Unless replaced, the `method` clause emits `Customer Payment Session Requested` or `Account Payment Instruction Created` once on initialization, carrying `paymentDetails`. On a matching `Payment Requested` event, it emits `MyOS Execution Requested` with the method, details and triggering request. These events describe creation or requested work; they do not confirm an external session, secured funds or a completed payment.
